To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the noncollinear collision of gravitational plane wave trains can lead to the formation of a naked singularity, and that the noncollinearity of the polarization vectors of the incoming waves can be used to avoid the formation of such singularities.

the head‐on collisions of gravitational plane waves can be described by an analytic four‐parameter family of exact solutions of the Einstein field equations, that this family includes the head‐on interaction of two plane waves with nonparallel polarization, and that in some cases this family contains models that avoid curvature singularities.

(1) the head‐on collisions of gravitational waves of noncollinear polarization can be described analytically, (2) the resulting spacetimes have no curvature singularity at their future boundary, and (3) the noncollinear character of the polarization is the direct cause of the singularity avoidance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the study of the interaction between gravitational plane waves.
the construction of a large class of new exact solutions of Einstein's field equations which represent the head-on collision of gravitational waves of arbitrary polarization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the noncollinear collision of plane waves with variable profile is the most promising class of models for the construction of nonsingular spacetimes.

the noncollinear nature of the polarization of gravitational waves is an important physical property, which has a significant effect on the dynamics of the interaction of such waves with other gravitational waves or with matter, and that the noncollinearity of the polarization of a gravitational plane wave is a sufficient condition for the avoidance of the curvature singularity at the future boundary of a region of interaction.

, in general, the singularity is avoided in the head‐on collisions of gravitational plane waves, and that, in particular, the singularity avoidance in the collision of waves with noncollinearpolarizations is due to the fact that the waves are not collinear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given profile, the noncollinear plane wave collision is a more effective singularity avoidance mechanism than the collinear one.

the inverse scattering method is an efficient tool for constructing exact solutions of Einstein's field equations and, in particular, for studying the collision of gravitational plane and shock waves.
we have obtained the exact solutions of Einstein's field equations for head‐on collision between gravitational plane waves with arbitrary polarization and profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the first time, a class of exact solutions has been found that is capable of modeling head‐on collisions of gravitational plane waves in the general case of noncollinear polarization.
the inverse scattering method can be used to construct exact models of head‐on collisions of gravitational plane waves, even when the polarization of the waves is not parallel.
the inverse scattering method provides a very useful tool for constructing exact solutions of Einstein equations with noncollinear plane wave polarization.
